title: 4×4 Box Breathing
clinicalIntent: An optional paced-breathing practice with even phases. You can skip pauses, choose a different rhythm, or leave your breathing natural.
contraindications: If changing or focusing on your breath feels uncomfortable, stop and let your breathing return to its natural rhythm. Choose another practice if breath focus does not feel right.

steps.label: Inhale
steps.description: If you want to follow the count, allow a comfortable inhale. No need to reach a particular number.

steps.label: Optional pause
steps.description: You may pause only if it feels comfortable. Skipping this pause is completely okay; let your breath continue naturally.

steps.label: Exhale
steps.description: If comfortable, allow an easy exhale. There is no need to make it longer or push the air out.

steps.label: Rest
steps.description: Let the next breath arrive in its own time, or skip this pause and breathe naturally.

aftercare: If you feel dizzy or uncomfortable, stop and let your breathing return to its natural rhythm. You can instead notice a neutral sound or object.
whenToEscalate: If you have new or severe breathing difficulty or chest pain, stop and seek urgent medical care. In the U.S. and its territories, call or text 988 for emotional crisis support. For immediate danger, contact local emergency services.

title: 5-4-3-2-1 Senses Grounding
clinicalIntent: An optional way to notice sensory details around you. Choose only the senses that feel comfortable and skip any that do not.
contraindications: If a sense or prompt feels uncomfortable, skip it or stop the practice.

steps.label: Things you see
steps.description: If looking around feels okay, gently notice one or more things you can see. You can keep your gaze on a neutral object.

steps.label: Things you feel
steps.description: If it feels comfortable, notice a point of contact such as clothing or the chair. No need to touch or move anything.

steps.label: Things you hear
steps.description: If listening feels okay, notice one or more sounds nearby or farther away.

steps.label: Things you smell
steps.description: You might notice a smell already present or remember a familiar one. Do not seek out a smell; skipping is okay.

steps.label: Things you taste
steps.description: If it feels comfortable, notice a taste already present or imagine one. You can skip this step.

aftercare: Take a few natural breaths. You can repeat this sequence if needed.
whenToEscalate: If you feel increasingly disconnected or distressed, stop and consider reaching out to someone you trust. In the U.S. and its territories, call or text 988 for emotional crisis support. For immediate danger, contact local emergency services.

title: Panic Anchoring: Feet and Breath
clinicalIntent: A brief set of optional grounding prompts for moments of intense stress. Choose the prompts that feel comfortable; no response or breath change is required.
contraindications: If a prompt increases distress or feels unsafe, skip it or stop the practice.

steps.label: Notice support
steps.description: If it feels okay, notice a surface supporting you. You do not need to move or press your feet down.

steps.label: Breath or another anchor
steps.description: You can let your breath be natural, notice a neutral sound, or skip this prompt. No breath pattern is required.

steps.label: Orient to one detail
steps.description: If looking around feels okay, notice one color, shape, or object. You do not need to decide whether your surroundings are safe.

aftercare: You can stop here, shift attention outward, or reach out to someone you trust. There is no need to make a feeling change quickly.
whenToEscalate: In the U.S. and its territories, call or text 988 for emotional crisis support. For immediate danger, contact local emergency services.

title: Anchoring Protocol
clinicalIntent: A few optional prompts to explore during an intense moment. You can choose an external anchor and leave breath or body focus out of the practice.
contraindications: If touch or breath focus does not feel comfortable, skip those prompts or stop.

steps.label: Choose an anchor
steps.description: If touch feels comfortable, rest a hand wherever you choose. You can also notice an object or sound instead.

steps.label: Notice, without changing
steps.description: Your breath can stay exactly as it is. If breath focus feels uncomfortable, return attention to a neutral object or sound.

steps.label: A simple point of attention
steps.description: You might notice one detail around you or count a few breaths if that feels okay. You can also skip this step.

aftercare: Keep, change, or leave your chosen anchor. You are free to end the practice here.
whenToEscalate: In the U.S. and its territories, call or text 988 for emotional crisis support. For immediate danger, contact local emergency services.

title: Standard Ritual Sequence
clinicalIntent: A short sequence of optional prompts for pausing and noticing the present. Nothing needs to change or be released.
contraindications: If a prompt feels uncomfortable, skip it or stop the practice.

steps.label: Pause and arrive
steps.description: Take a moment to pause and arrive in this space. No rush.

steps.label: Pause
steps.description: You might notice your breath as it is, or choose a sound or object instead.

steps.label: Notice, or skip
steps.description: If body awareness feels comfortable, notice one sensation. You can keep your attention outside your body instead.

steps.label: End in your own way
steps.description: Nothing needs to be released. You can stay as you are, shift attention, or finish the practice.

aftercare: Notice how you feel. You can repeat the sequence if helpful.
whenToEscalate: If you experience increased distress or dissociation, stop and reach out for support. Call 988 (U.S.) if in crisis.

title: Hand-on-Heart Shame Soften
clinicalIntent: Optional self-compassion prompts for when self-criticism feels strong. Use only the words or contact that feel comfortable.
contraindications: If touch feels unsafe, use a soft object or imagine the gesture. Proceed only as far as feels okay.

steps.label: Choose contact or space
steps.description: If touch feels comfortable, rest a hand somewhere you choose or hold a soft object. Imagining it or skipping is okay too.

steps.label: A point of attention
steps.description: You can let your breath be natural, notice an object, or skip this prompt. No breathing pattern is needed.

steps.label: Optional kind words
steps.description: If words feel useful, you might try: 'This is a hard moment.' You do not need to repeat or believe any phrase.

steps.label: Finish or continue
steps.description: You can end now, stay with your chosen anchor, or move your attention to something neutral around you.

aftercare: Language must never blame. All phrases should validate experience, not dismiss it.
whenToEscalate: If shame intensifies or you feel increasingly isolated, reach out to a trusted person or professional. Call 988 (U.S.) if you are in danger or considering self-harm.

title: Grief Wave Seat
clinicalIntent: Optional reflection prompts for grief. There is no need to revisit memories or stay with an emotion; you can pause, shift attention, or stop.
contraindications: If grief feels overwhelming or destabilizing, pause and seek support. This is not exposure therapy.

steps.label: Choose what feels manageable
steps.description: You can stay where you are, adjust your position, or skip this practice altogether.

steps.label: Name or notice
steps.description: If it feels okay, use a word for what is present. You do not need to revisit a memory or explain anything.

steps.label: Choose an anchor
steps.description: You might notice a neutral object, a sound, or your natural breathing. Shift away from grief whenever you want.

steps.label: Set your own limit
steps.description: You can stop now or continue only while it feels manageable. There is nothing to resolve in this practice.

aftercare: Permission to stop at any time. This is accompaniment, not endurance. Be gentle with yourself.
whenToEscalate: If grief becomes overwhelming or you feel unable to cope, stop and reach out for support. Call 988 (U.S.) if you are in danger or considering self-harm.

title: Orienting Protocol
clinicalIntent: Optional sensory prompts to explore at your own pace. You can keep your attention on one neutral detail or stop at any time.
contraindications: If orienting increases distress, stop and try a simpler anchor (e.g., feet on floor, one breath).

steps.label: Orient if you choose
steps.description: If looking around feels comfortable, notice one color or shape. You do not need to decide whether anything is safe.

steps.label: Notice one object
steps.description: You might name one object you can see, or keep your gaze on a neutral spot. There is no target number.

steps.label: Notice support or sound
steps.description: If it feels okay, notice a surface supporting you or a sound nearby. No need to move or press your feet down.

aftercare: You can repeat the feet-on-ground step as often as needed.
whenToEscalate: If you feel increasingly disconnected or unsafe, stop and reach out to a trusted person. Call 988 (U.S.) if in crisis.
